Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: Vitamin D level was significantly related to risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5) six months after COVID-19 hospital admission; the direction is not stated in the abstract.
Sentence: "The variables that were significantly related to the risk of depression 6 months after admission for COVID-19 were frailty (p = 0.006 for pre-frail and p = 0.001 for frail), small-vessel vascular disease in imaging tests (p = 0.033), vitamin D level (p = 0.006), and taking antidepressants (p = 0.011)."
Measured as: risk of depression (PHQ-9 above 5)
Population: 72 patients admitted to a hospital in Spain for COVID-19, assessed at discharge and six months later
Intervention: Serum vitamin D level (measured, not administered)
Comparator: Lower versus higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 72
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: The depression group had significantly lower vitamin D levels than healthy controls.
Sentence: "Elevated levels of CRP (p = 0.0038), hs-CRP (p = 0.0048), and IL-6 (p = 0.0030) were identified in the anxiety group, while the depression group was characterized by reduced vitamin D levels (p = 0.0302)."
Measured as: depression group (vs control) vitamin D levels
Population: 50 volunteers: healthy controls and individuals with anxiety, depression or bipolar disorder
Intervention: No intervention; serum vitamin D measured cross-sectionally
Comparator: Healthy control group
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 50
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Both are observational vitamin D level studies, but Study A's direction is unstated and its outcome is depression risk 6 months after COVID-19 versus a cross-sectional case-control comparison, so the findings do not clearly conflict.","verdict":"apparent","reason":"outcome_measure","also_differs":["population","design_or_bias"],"detail":"Study A: PHQ-9 >5 risk in post-COVID inpatients, direction not stated; Study B: vitamin D level in a depression group vs controls, cross-sectional, n = 50"}
